proof:
# A strictly convex ambient body gives finite-fiber compatibility slack

Let C be a strictly convex body in R^n x R^d, d>=1, and suppose
its mixed d-volume is positive. Let P be the finite set of ALL
nonempty integer fibers K_z=C_z. Positive-volume fibers are full
d-dimensional bodies; zero-volume fibers are retained below.

There is a number epsilon>0 such that the following independent
perturbations are compatible. For every positive-volume fiber choose
ANY compact convex body K'_z with d_H(K'_z,K_z)<epsilon. Leave every
zero-volume fiber unchanged. Then

    conv(union_(z in P) {z} x K'_z)

has exactly fiber K'_z at every integer z in P and has no other
nonempty integer fibers. The claim concerns convex-hull fiber
identities; a full ambient convex-body realization is supplied in
Section 3 even if P has a lower-dimensional affine span.

This local openness statement does not assert attainment of a depth
infimum in a class of strictly convex bodies, and its slack need not
stay bounded away from zero along approximating sequences.

## 1. Strict containment for representations excluding the target

Fix z in P. Define the finite representation polytope

    R_z={lambda_p>=0 (p in P minus {z}):
         sum lambda_p=1, sum lambda_p p=z}.

If it is empty, no compatibility constraint at z is needed. Otherwise
every representation has at least two positive coefficients at
DISTINCT base points. For any choices x_p in K_p, strict convexity
of the ambient C implies

    (z,sum lambda_p x_p) belongs to int C.               (1)

To justify finite combinations, combine two positively weighted
distinct-base points first. Their strict intermediate point is in
int C by strict convexity. A convex combination of an interior point
with points of C, retaining positive weight on the interior point,
remains interior. Thus (1) follows.

In particular K_z must have positive d-volume whenever R_z is
nonempty. Thus every zero-volume integer fiber has its base as a
vertex of conv P and cannot be produced from the other bases.

Let lambda^1,...,lambda^N be the finitely many vertices of a nonempty
R_z. Each compact Minkowski interpolant

    A_j=sum_(p!=z) lambda^j_p K_p

lies in int K_z by (1), and hence A_j+delta_j B_d subset K_z for
some delta_j>0. Set delta_z=min_j delta_j>0. If lambda is any
convex combination sum alpha_j lambda^j, distributivity of convex
Minkowski sums gives

    sum_p lambda_p K_p = sum_j alpha_j A_j.

Therefore

    (sum_p lambda_p K_p)+delta_z B_d subset K_z
                  for EVERY lambda in R_z.              (2)

The distributivity equality uses convexity of each K_p; multiple
scaled copies of a convex set combine to their total scalar multiple.
Formula (2) is a uniform inward slack for representations EXCLUDING
the target fiber. Allowing its own coefficient to approach one would
destroy such a uniform statement, which is why that coefficient has
been removed from R_z.

## 2. Independent small perturbations preserve all integer slices

There are finitely many nonempty R_z. If any exist, choose epsilon
smaller than half the minimum of their delta_z; otherwise choose any
positive epsilon. All positive original fibers have an inball, so
epsilon can also be decreased below half their minimum inradius.
The latter is optional if full-dimensionality of each K'_z is
already assumed, as in the statement.

For any representation lambda in R_z, the corresponding perturbed
interpolant lies within Hausdorff distance epsilon of the original
one, since sum lambda_p=1 and each summand moves by at most epsilon.
Consequently (2) gives

    sum_p lambda_p K'_p subset K_z eroded by (delta_z-epsilon)B_d.

Hausdorff distance at most epsilon between compact convex bodies
implies |h_(K'_z)(u)-h_(K_z)(u)|<=epsilon for unit u. Hence K'_z
contains K_z eroded by epsilon B_d: every point in that erosion
satisfies u.x<=h_(K_z)(u)-epsilon<=h_(K'_z)(u) for all unit u.
Since delta_z-epsilon>epsilon, it follows that

    sum_p lambda_p K'_p subset K'_z.                    (3)

Any convex combination with total base z that also uses K'_z either
uses that fiber alone, or, after removing and renormalizing its own
coefficient, uses a representation from R_z. Convexity of K'_z and
(3) therefore put the whole combination in K'_z. Conversely K'_z
is one of the generating fibers, proving the exact fiber identity.
For zero-volume targets R_z is empty, so the identity is automatic.

Finally conv(P) intersect Z^n=P, because conv(P) is contained in the
projection of C and every integer point of that projection has a
nonempty C fiber. The perturbed hull has projection conv(P), so it
has no integer fibers outside P.

## 3. Full ambient realization when the base span is deficient

If aff P has dimension n, the perturbed hull is already a convex
body in R^(n+d): its base span is full and at least one source fiber
has dimension d. Otherwise let E be the direction space of aff P,
and let D_eta be the radius-eta ball in E-perp, viewed as integer-
coordinate vectors (no lattice coordinate change is performed).
Add D_eta x {0} to the perturbed hull.

For sufficiently small eta>0 the new projection conv(P)+D_eta has
no integer points outside P. Indeed all its possible integer points
lie in one bounded set, hence form a finite list. An integer point
outside aff P has positive perpendicular distance from aff P; choose
eta smaller than the finitely many such distances. Points in aff P
belong to conv(P)+D_eta only if they already belong to conv(P),
because the perpendicular summand must vanish.

For the same reason, at each base z in P the perpendicular summand
must be zero. Thus this thickening preserves every desired fiber
K'_z exactly. It makes the body full dimensional. To see the needed
relative full dimensionality before thickening, take one full
d-dimensional fiber and base points spanning aff P; their affine
differences together with the continuous fiber directions span
E x R^d. Adding E-perp completes the ambient space.

This realization retains zero-volume boundary fibers as well as all
positive fibers. It is not claimed to remain strictly convex after
arbitrary independent perturbations and the final perpendicular
thickening; its purpose is exact membership in the class of induced
convex-body fiber families.

# A strictly convex ambient body gives finite-fiber compatibility slack

**Finite fiber compatibility slack inside a strict ambient body**

Let C be a strictly convex body, d>=1, with positive mixed d-volume, and let P be all its nonempty integer fibers K_z. For each z, every convex representation of z using only P\{z} has its represented fiber sum strictly inside C at base z; compactness of these representation polytopes gives a common positive slack for the positive-volume target fibers. Consequently all positive-volume K_z can be independently replaced by sufficiently small Hausdorff perturbations that remain compact convex d-bodies, while every zero-volume fiber is kept fixed, and the resulting family is realized by a convex body with exactly the prescribed integer fibers. The realizing body is not asserted to remain strictly convex.

Scope limits: Slack depends on the given body and fiber family; it is not uniform along approximation sequences. The realizing body need not remain strictly convex.
